book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.c: Directional attacks, defense, combos, and configuration
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.b: An introduction to lock-on and directional combat
Use the lock-on key to select a target. Move the mouse to change attack direction. Attacking, blocking, and dodging consume stamina. Attack direction affects your next stance and available combos.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.c: Combos trigger when your recent attack directions match a learned sequence. The sequence is checked from the newest hits, so choose each direction before attacking and keep pressure without breaking the chain. Data packs may restrict a combo with required_weapon_tag; common values include swords, short_swords, longswords, axes, pickaxes, fighting_maces, maces, and heavy_weapons. heavy_weapons includes fighting maces, axes, and pickaxes.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.d: Combat data is loaded from data/<namespace>/kingdom_come_combat/. Data packs can extend or override combos, moves, weapons, armor, mobs, ai, passive_skills, and skill_books. Configuration is read again when data packs reload.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.a: How to obtain the manual, skills, and skill books

With Modonomicon installed, shapelessly craft a book and an iron sword to obtain the Kingdom Come Combat Manual, then use it in hand. Skill books are separate unlock items for one combo or book-sourced passive. Find them in ruins, temples, stronghold libraries, woodland mansions, ancient cities, and trial rewards, or buy them from level 2, 4, and 5 librarians. Open a skill book and turn to page two to learn it. Press K (rebindable) to review learned combos, passives, and skills purchasable with experience.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.s: The shared resource for offense, defense, and movement

Players have 100 base maximum stamina. Attacks use their move cost, dodges cost 18, forward steps cost 7, and normal blocks cost stamina based on incoming impact and block mitigation. Regeneration starts about two seconds after spending stamina at 1.2 per tick by default. Low health reduces maximum stamina, down to 60%; armor, injuries, weapons, shields, and skills can modify costs or recovery. Exhaustion weakens armor panels and can break guards, so avoid empty swings.

Blocking works from the front. Tap block shortly before impact to open a perfect-block window; without classic mode, the block direction must match the incoming attack. Shields add a larger perfect-block window and can passively catch attacks, but heavy shields increase some stamina costs. A normal block spends stamina from incoming impact after weapon or shield mitigation. If you cannot pay the cost, the guard fails and the hit continues. Perfect blocks drain and stagger the attacker, open a counter window, and do not use the same stamina calculation as a normal block.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.i: Localized wounds, bleeding, bandages, and recovery

Hits can injure arms, hands, torso, legs, or head; bleeding deals periodic damage. Equip bandages in matching armor slots: head for head wounds, chest for torso/arm/hand wounds, and legs for leg wounds. Bandages stop bleeding first, then reduce wounds one layer at a time down to one remaining layer while losing durability. Level 1-3 wounds naturally recover roughly once per ten minutes; ordinary healing accelerates this, and sleeping can spend food to treat minor wounds.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.t: Perfect defense, master strikes, and practical tactics

Read the incoming direction, then tap block shortly before impact with the matching direction. The base perfect-block window is 12 ticks; shields add 8 ticks. Success drains the attacker, disables their attack for about a second, and opens a brief counter window. For a master strike, attack in the same direction during roughly the first 8 ticks of an enemy attack while within two blocks. Preserve stamina, avoid misses, step forward against retreating targets, and dodge attacks that are unsafe to block.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.p: Thrust, strike, slash, and posture pressure

Damage is split into thrust, strike, and slash. Thrust represents points and narrow penetration, slash represents cutting edges, and strike represents blunt force. Weapons, projectiles, moves, enchantments, durability, and hit location combine into those three incoming values. Armor compares each value against its matching defense panel for the covered body part, so a helmet may stop slash while still letting some strike or thrust through. Impact is separate posture pressure that drains stamina and can interrupt actions; blocked strike damage can still become impact.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.a: Coverage, three defense panels, and durability

Armor protects only configured body parts. On hit, thrust, strike, and slash penetration are compared separately against the matching defense of armor covering that location, then scaled by part protection. Multiple layers retain the best reduction for each type. Impact mitigation separately reduces stamina pressure up to 95%. Wear, low stamina, and armor-breach effects weaken defense; attacks damage the most effective protective layer. Aim for gaps or choose a damage type suited to the target.

The new armor system uses data-driven coverage, three defense panels, part protection, burden, impact mitigation, durability wear, and low-stamina weakening instead of relying only on vanilla armor value. Enchantments can feed those panels too: Heavy adds strike damage, Pointed adds thrust damage, and Sharpness still contributes weapon damage. Cushioning improves armor impact mitigation. Bracers copies an armor piece's shoulder protection panel to its arm coverage, replacing any existing arm panel. Stable, Powerful, and Rapid Fire modify ranged weapon handling.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.p: Apply potion effects to weapons and arrows

Hold a usable potion in the offhand and a valid weapon or at least four arrows in the main hand, then use the main hand. The coating action uses a bow-like third-person pose and takes about three seconds. Coating arrows consumes four arrows and the potion, then returns tipped arrows. Coating a weapon stores the potion on the weapon for a limited number of damaging hits; strong enough hits transfer a shortened version of the potion effects to the target. Empty bottles are returned through the normal inventory flow.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.g: Kingdom Come Combat adds four world game rules. Use /gamerule kccClassicMode true to make player perfect blocks less direction strict and allow a short held normal block. Use /gamerule kccCombatSpeed <value> to multiply player and mob combat animation speed; it is clamped from 0.05 to 10.0 and stacks with weapon, armor, and skill speed modifiers.

/gamerule kccTrauma controls player injury, bleeding, and treatment consequences; mobs still use their combat behavior even when player trauma is disabled. /gamerule kccHardcoreMode hides lock-on crosshair aids and is automatically enabled when a vanilla hardcore server starts. These rules are saved per world, so data packs can tune combat while server owners keep final control.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.h: Momentum, stamina, braking, and sprint taps

Horses now use momentum and their own stamina. Tap sprint to build speed; holding movement keeps the horse moving forward while left and right steer the horse instead of instantly strafing. Turning is slower at high speed, and turning while moving reduces speed. Running above the threshold drains horse stamina, while walking or resting restores it. Jumping and hard braking cost stamina. If stamina reaches zero, the horse stops and needs a short recovery; overdriving speed too far can panic the horse and throw the rider.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.c: Combo finishers are more than alternate animations. They can redirect the hit to a specific part such as face, crown, abdomen, or knee; adjust thrust, strike, and slash multipliers; add armor-breaking pressure; interrupt the target; or apply a short movement lock. Some combos are broad finishing cuts for groups, some punish exposed heads, and some target joints or armor gaps. A combo only triggers after it is learned; use the K skills screen to see the current data-pack values and inputs.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.l: Longsword use, material tiers, and recipes

Longswords have extended reach and unlock dedicated two-handed techniques. Wood, stone, copper, gold, iron, diamond, and netherite variants share one recipe: place the material in the top-center slot, fill the middle row with three of the same material, and place a stick in the bottom-center slot. Material tier changes base attack and durability; thrust, strike, slash, and weapon condition still shape final performance.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.f: Heavy mace use, material tiers, and recipes

Fighting maces are heavy weapons built around strike damage, armor breaking, and impact. They can use heavy weapon combos and are suited to armored targets that resist clean cuts. Copper, gold, iron, diamond, and netherite variants share one recipe: leave the top-left empty, place material in the top-center and top-right, place a stick in the center and material in the middle-right, then place a stick in the bottom-left. There are no wooden or stone fighting maces.

The hand cannon is a high-power ranged weapon. Hold firearm cartridges in the offhand and use the cannon in the main hand to load it; use it again after loading to fire. Loading leaves you vulnerable. Craft the cannon from five iron ingots and a stick. One iron nugget and one gunpowder shapelessly craft four cartridges. Projectiles use their own thrust, strike, and slash panels against armor covering the hit part. Headshots are resolved through the same localized system, so a shot can strike protected crown or side-head areas, while an exposed face is far more dangerous.
